articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Video Reveals Major Change That Could End Wallhacks for Good
articles.summary: Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4, Activision has a plan to change that. If you're unfamiliar with the term, wallhacks are a type of cheat that allows nefarious players to see their opponents' every move through walls.
body: As detailed in a new video published on the franchise's official social media pages, publisher Activision and developer Infinity Ward revealed a new system aimed at combating wallhack cheaters. Called "server culling," the goal is to make Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 more reliable – and fair – than ever before.

The relatively in-depth explanation touches on how cheaters have been able to use wallhacks thus far. Usually, servers share information, such as a player's in-game location, between game clients. It means that, even when you can't see an enemy hiding behind cover, waiting to pop out for an easy kill, the game itself still recognizes that the player is there.

Server culling, which saw Infinity Ward build occlusion layers into Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's environments, essentially limits information to what the player is able to see. So, if you can't see someone behind the wall, the backend can't either – and that goes for wallhackers, too.
"For legitimate players, the match plays exactly as intended," Activision explained. "For cheat developers, this creates a major new obstacle."
points: Wallhacks have plagued Call of Duty for years, but in Modern Warfare 4, Activision has a plan to change that.

articles.title: 'Game Changer' Season 9 Will Have "Unexplainable" Games, Dropout CEO Sam Reich Reveals
articles.summary: Dropout CEO Sam Reich chats with Polygon about lessons he's learned from eight seasons of Game Changer and how the Topeka trip almost didn't happen.
body: For a moment, Dropout CEO and Game Changer host Sam Reich wondered if he could get away with not going to Topeka, Kansas.

The Game Changer season 8 episode “What’s the Catch” starts as if the episode is all about handing out prizes, but those prizes quickly get a “catch” that turns them into punishments. At one point, one of contestant Jacob Wysocki’s “prizes” turns into a private improv show where Sam drives him around. Eventually, it gets the catch of having to take place in Topeka, Kansas, and suddenly the tormentor also becomes the tormented. Reich and Wysocki are forced on a trip to Topeka for the most random improv show inside their rented car.
“There was a moment between Jacob and I after the fact where we talked about faking it,” Reich tells Polygon.
Dropout considered just pretending to go to Kansas for the bit, but worried that the Game Changer audience would know. Ultimately, Reich decided not to go down that path.

articles.title: 'I Did My Best' — Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Director Responds to Fans Asking for Full Disc Version
articles.summary: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Naoki Hamaguchi said he did his best to fight for a disc release as the industry heads toward a "future where physical media is essentially disc-less."
body: The lead developer in charge of next year's new remake chapter opened up about the state of gaming during an interview with Radio Times. It's a topic he's touched on before, but this time, he explained how his own appreciation for physical media led him to push for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation to get at least one disc as the industry speeds toward an all-digital future.

"Personally, obviously, I bought lots of physical editions of games as a child. Sometimes I buy digital editions of games, but if I'm particularly attached to a title, I want to get the physical version," Hamaguchi said, noting how the topic of a fully digital future has become "particularly sensitive" in recent months. "And you know, being in the industry, sometimes I want to get my friends or acquaintances who've worked on something to sign a copy of their own game."

articles.title: The 8 Best Games Like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
articles.summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is one of, if not the best, RPGs of all time. 11 years after launch, everyone's playing it again thanks to a fancy new remaster (that's free for anyone who owns the existing game), meant to prep players for the Songs of the Past expansion that's in the works.
body: The Witcher 3 has plenty of defining traits: a beautiful, dense open world; side quests with narratives so enrapturing they're better than most games' main stories; larger-than-life characters who become so personable, you'd consider them friends; and combat mechanics that allow you to dance between foes, all while using two swords and magic at once.
If any of that sounds like your sort of thing, here are the eight best games like The Witcher 3.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is the newest game on this list, and it comes from studio Rebel Wolves, which is led by The Witcher 3 game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz. The studio also employs a number of other former high-level staffers from CD Projekt Red, and as a result, it's one of the closest games you'll find to matching what Geralt's best adventure has to offer.

In The Blood of Dawnwalker, you are Coen. He's part-vampire, part-witch, a.k.a. a Dawnwalker. Not a Witcher. Structurally, however, this is heavily inspired by The Witcher games: a stunning open world with so many side quests to find, innovative, direction-based, parry-focused combat, and a unique time-based mechanic where every decision truly matters.
points: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is one of, if not the best, RPGs of all time.

articles.title: Ace Combat 8 Secretly Has the Best Video Game Music of the Year
articles.summary: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the best video games I’ve played in 2026, and there are plenty of reasons why. It has airtight flying controls, features a diversity of thrilling missions, revitalizes a series that’s been silent for years, and happens to be one of the best-looking games of…
body: That claim will only come as a surprise if you’re not familiar with the Ace Combat series. Long-time fans have always known that the Ace Combat series’ music is one of its best qualities. That’s thanks in part to composer Keiki Kobayashi, whose soaring orchestral compositions give the series’ aerial missions a sense of grandeur. This time around, Kobayashi worked alongside Ryo Watanabe and Mitsuhiro Kitadani to create the series’ best score yet.
Don’t take it from me. Take six minutes to listen to the game’s main theme, “Everflow.” Though be warned that it will make you feel like you can run through a wall.

The word “epic” gets overused a lot in video game culture, but it’s really the only way to describe the compositions in Ace Combat 8. Each one feels enormous in scope, filled with choirs that feel impossibly large and string sections that drag a bow across your heart. They get your blood pumping during tense missions, but they also are emotionally charged enough to add some real weight to the war you’re fighting. It evokes the blockbuster sounds of the Metal Gear Solid soundtrack.
points: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve is one of the best video games I’ve played in 2026, and there are plenty of reasons why.

articles.title: Sony in talks to land Battlefield movie from Christopher McQuarrie and Michael B. Jordan
articles.summary: Sony is reportedly in talks to acquire a big-screen adaptation of Electronic Arts' Battlefield, with Christopher McQuarrie attached to write, direct and produce, and Michael B. Jordan on board to produce.
body: As reported by Variety, Sony declined to comment on the negotiations, which reportedly followed a bidding war between multiple studios.

Jordan, fresh off his Best Actor Oscar win, could also end up starring in the film, though Variety notes that's dependent on several factors. Additional producers named include EA's Jesse Stern, Emerald Neon's Carter Swan, Vertigo's Roy Lee and Miri Yoon, and Outlier Society's Elizabeth Raposo.

Battlefield launched in 2002. The series' 18th mainline instalment, Battlefield 6, arrived last year and went on to become the bestselling first-person shooter of the year, and of the franchise's history, reportedly outselling Call of Duty ( which is getting its own film treatment, of course, with Peter Berg directing a Taylor Sheridan script for Paramount, dated for release on 30th June 2028).

Battlefield recently unveiled Rapid Royale, Redsec's version of Warzone's Resurgence. Resurgence takes place on dedicated maps that are far smaller than the main mode's large playground, and offers many ways to respawn after death. The pace is significantly faster with more frequent firefights as a result.

articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Doesn't Have to Be a Slog
articles.summary: I admire Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave approach to bigness. What stood out to me during the review period and since is how many ways it lets you tailor free time and some battles to your needs, even if that tailoring means skipping certain things entirely.
body: Fortune's Weave throws a lot at you when you get free time between Heroic Games matches. The world map is gigantic and enticingly blank, tempting you to explore every corner. There's a bunch of side quests. Monsters roam, dungeons loom, and treasures idle in their designated spots, waiting for you to find them. If you spent every turn of free time exploring and fighting and pulling vegetables out of the ground, yes, Fortune's Weave would be an unbearable, fatuous game, Nintendo's concession to the worst tendencies of modern game design.
A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

articles.title: The Witcher 3's remaster just brought it to a new all-time concurrent player count peak
articles.summary: It's hard to believe it's been over a decade since The Witcher 3 first released, and even harder to believe they found a way to make Geralt's tub transformation even shinier.
body: The new screaming high is a whopping 123,359, which it just reached an hour ago as I write this. It's settling down now, but still pretty impressive given that its peak in August was just over 30,000. The game might be getting on in years, but it's still one of the best in its genre.

When PC Gamer's Shaun Prescott first reviewed it in 2015, he scored the game a mighty 92% and called it "a big, beautiful, sprawling action RPG full of rich stories, and suffused with an oppressive darkness."

It may not have been a huge stride forward for the style, instead feeling like innumerable tiny steps: a bar-setting journey through Andrzej Sapkowski's setting with all the graceful execution of an Olympic gold medalist's platform dive. "The Witcher 3 doesn’t bring much that’s bracingly new to the modern RPG. It’s a series of refinements," he wrote.

articles.title: Capcom plans to evolve RE Engine into an "AI-generation game engine"
articles.summary: Capcom wants to transform its in-house RE Engine into what it's calling an "AI-generation game engine".
body: As reported by gamebiz (via VGC ), programmer Satoshi Ishida outlined the plans at the "Capcom Open Conference RE:2026" event yesterday (2nd October), explaining that the changes were coming as part of an ongoing overhaul dubbed the REX Project.
RE Engine has been in development since 2014 and made its debut in Resident Evil 7 back in 2017. It's since been the engine behind the best part of 30 Capcom titles.

Ishida pointed to three challenges driving the REX Project – one, games have grown so large in scope and data volume that build and iteration times are slowing development down; two, RE Engine is now used by over 2,000 developers, including international staff and people coming from other engines, requiring better multilingual and accessibility support; and three, AI needs to be built into the development pipeline rather than bolted on.

That's why Capcom intends to bundle several new systems into the REX Project, including RE:Dox, which standardises data processing across formats, RE:UI, which speeds up development tools by separating appearance from state, and RE:Log, which swaps text-based logging for an ID-based system.
points: Capcom wants to transform its in-house RE Engine into what it's calling an "AI-generation game engine".

articles.title: Has your life ever been changed by someone you met in an MMO?
articles.summary: Terminally Online. This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about…
body: WoW: Forever's had me nostalgic for a bygone era of MMOs that seems to be enjoying a touch of a resurgence—the idea of a lived-in immersive world, versus the daily task theme park of modern MMO design. Not that I have anything against the latter, mind. Theme parks are neat and roller coasters are fun.

But I have, true to the point, been grouping up with strangers more often in a slower-burn world, partially for convenience, but also partially because the slower pace has me less hungry for rampant progress and time saving. I've gotta hike for six minutes to get to this quest anyway, why wouldn't I stop and help someone in trouble?

When I get all sappy and soft-hearted like this, I also think of The Remarkable Life of Ibelin, a documentary about a WoW player Mats Steen, who sadly died in 2014 of Duchenne muscular dystrophy—a man whose closest online friends travelled from across the world to attend his funeral.

articles.title: Memory shortages set to persist into 2028, warns Micron CEO
articles.summary: Micron has warned that global RAM shortages show no sign of easing, telling investors on its earnings call that it has already sold most of next year's production.
body: As reported by The Register, CEO and chair Sanjay Mehrotra suggested customers should brace for prices well above what they paid in 2026, adding demand would keep outstripping supply through 2027 and into 2028, and calling the industry's supply-demand balance "only getting tighter".
The CEO also admitted that Micron does "not have line of sight to when supply and demand will return to balance".

As most of the capacity is booked for the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) needed for AI datacentres, the big three memory manufacturers - which includes Samsung - have very little dedicated to consumer-grade memory, which caused their prices to shoot up.

That has, in turn, pushed up the prices of pretty much every consumer electronic device that uses these chips, including game consoles like the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S and Switch 2 - all of which have gone up in price several times in some cases. Valve's Steam Machine also launched at a much higher price than Valve expected, and the company hinted it may even have to raise prices again.
points: Micron has warned that global RAM shortages show no sign of easing, telling investors on its earnings call that it has already sold most of next year's production.
